why: A monoline laptop screen with an email: an attachment icon labelled customer list, a cursor hovering over Send, then stopping.
The presenter speaks beside three outlined labels, each in its class colour, appearing as each class is named.
A large question mark over a document outline; a file-type badge and a folder icon fade back as the narration says they do not decide.
A monoline press release page gets an approved tick, its outline turns the public colour and it slides out to the open world.
A meeting notes page sits beside the press release; its outline turns the internal colour as internal is said.
The internal notes move toward the outline of the building's door and stop at it; they stay inside.
The opening customer list returns, rows of names drawn as lines; the harm question is applied and its outline turns the confidential colour.
The confidential list travels one protected line to a single named recipient, rests in a locked folder outline, then a paper copy is shredded and a file deleted.
Three uncoloured outline items appear one by one above three empty trays in the class colours.
Each item drops into its tray and takes the class colour; the org chart hovers over public, then settles in internal.
One confidential document turns from a printed page to a folder to a screen, its outline keeping the confidential colour throughout.
The rule large: an item with a dashed, uncertain outline steps up one class colour and an arrow points to an owner icon.
The opening email returns; the attachment's outline now shows the confidential colour, the cursor leaves Send and moves to a protected channel option.
